betterCitation: Etty Hillesum, Etty: The Letters and Diaries of Etty Hillesum 1941 to 1943, 26 August 1941 (trans. Arnold J. Pomerans, 2002)
reason: Refuted on the page number, not on the line. The wording and the date hold up: several independent readings this run return There is a really deep well inside me. And in it dwells God. Sometimes I am there, too., including the really and the comma before too, continuing But more often stones and grit block the well, and God is buried beneath. Then He must be dug out again., and all of them date the entry 26 August 1941. Attribution is right, the tag Diary is the form of the work, scope is clean since a private diary is not scripture and the Dutch originals are of 1981 and 1986, shipped.js reports not shipped, nothing near, Etty Hillesum at 1 of 3 for the year in month 2, not banned, and the source line leads with the name and carries no dash and no straight double quote. What fails is p. 91. Every attestation of that page I could reach traces back to one tertiary source, the Wikiquote page the evidence itself cites, and the mirrors that copy it; the verifier's own evidence records that two archive.org full text endpoints against the scans returned nothing, and my own attempts at the archive search inside endpoints were refused as well, so no copy of the named 2002 Eerdmans edition was opened by anyone in this chain. The brief is explicit that a locatable entry in a standard reference is a fame signal and never a verification, and this track's whole standard is that a confident false citation is worse than an honest hedge. A specific page asserted on the strength of a quotation site is that failure exactly, and one competing source seen this run gives page 97 for the same passage in an unspecified edition, which shows the number is not stable in the secondary literature. The fix is cheap and costs the card nothing: drop the page. For a diary the dated entry IS the locator rule 4 asks for, the better citation above is 124 characters, and it makes no claim that was not verified. Two corrections to the note, which also should not ship as written. First, the note treats Arno Pomerans and Arnold J. Pomerans as a disagreement among trade listings about the translator's name. They are the same man: Arnold Julius Pomerans, 1920 to 2005, the German born British translator from the Dutch, who was credited both ways across his roughly two hundred books. So the stated reason for moving off An Interrupted Life is partly an error, and the wording of this passage is reported the same in the 1983 An Interrupted Life as in the 2002 complete edition. Second, what the note says about An Interrupted Life being an abridgement is correct and worth keeping, since Het verstoorde leven of 1981 is a selection and the 2002 Etty is the complete and unabridged edition, so naming the complete edition is still the better choice, just without the page.
